Wise alternatives in 2026: how the options compare

By the Ibanora teamPublished November 16, 20268 min read

In short

Wise alternatives include Revolut, Payoneer, Airwallex, OFX and a bank wire from Bank of America. They charge in different ways: monthly plans, percentage fees, flat wire fees or a margin inside the exchange rate. Of the five, only Payoneer lists stablecoin payments on its pricing page. Figures are from each provider's own page as of November 2026.

A Wise alternative is any provider that does one of the jobs Wise does: sending money abroad, holding several currencies in one account, or running a company's international payments. Revolut, Payoneer, Airwallex, OFX and Bank of America each cover part of that list, and each charges in its own way. Every figure here comes from the provider's own website as of November 2026.

What Wise charges, and why people compare

As of November 2026, Wise charges a fee on each transfer or conversion and uses the mid-market rate. Its US pricing page says the fee varies by currency, starts from 0.23%, and comes with no subscriptions or plans. As an example, a 0.23% fee on a $1,000 conversion is $2.30. The percentage for your currency pair may be higher.

The Wise account page says you can hold 40 currencies and get account details for 20 of them. The pricing page lists free account details to receive in 22 currencies, so check the current list for the currency you need. For companies, the Wise Business pricing page lists a one-time setup fee of 31 USD, which includes account details. All of this is as of November 2026.

Crypto is mostly off the table at Wise. As of November 2026, its help article on cryptocurrency says Wise does not support buying, exchanging or trading cryptocurrencies, and that personal customers cannot send money from their account to crypto exchanges such as Coinbase or Binance. The same article says Wise cards can be used for any lawful transaction supported in the card region, including on crypto platforms.

What to compare when you leave Wise

  • The fee model. As of November 2026, Wise charges per transfer. Other providers use a monthly plan, a percentage above the interbank rate, a flat wire fee or a margin built into the rate. Work out the total cost on the amount you actually send.
  • Currencies you can hold. Each provider counts differently. As of November 2026, Airwallex says its Global Accounts hold 20+ currencies and OFX says 30+.
  • Account details. Local account details let a client or platform pay you as if you had an account in their country. Check that the currencies you invoice in are on the list.
  • Business tools, such as team cards, batch payments, a monthly allowance of ACH transfers and pricing per user.
  • Crypto and stablecoin access. A stablecoin is a digital token designed to hold a steady value against a currency such as the US dollar. As of November 2026, Wise accounts cannot be used to buy or trade crypto, and most of the providers below do not mention it on their pricing pages.

How each alternative to Wise charges

Revolut

As of November 2026, Revolut's US Standard fee schedule (last updated April 30, 2026) lists no subscription charge for the Standard plan. Exchanges use a rate based on foreign-exchange market rates. A customer whose base currency is USD can exchange up to $1,000 a month at that rate. Above that, Standard customers pay a fair usage fee of 0.5% on the extra amount.

As an example, converting $3,000 in one month during foreign-exchange market hours means $2,000 goes over the allowance, and 0.5% of $2,000 is $10. As of November 2026, the schedule adds a 1.0% fee outside foreign-exchange market hours, which it defines as 5:00pm Friday to 6:00pm Sunday Eastern Time.

As of November 2026, transfers abroad in the recipient's local currency cost 0.15% with a $0.75 minimum, and transfers in a different currency cost up to $6.00. When a local-currency route is not available, the "Pay All Transfer Fees" option applies: a $30 flat fee meant to cover both the Revolut fee and any intermediary bank fees. The fee schedule does not say how many currencies you can hold or whether US customers can buy crypto.

Payoneer

Payoneer's pricing page starts with the fees for receiving money. As of November 2026, payments from another Payoneer customer's balance and payments into a local-currency receiving account are free. A non-local-currency receiving account costs 1% (minimum 1.00 USD), and a client paying by credit card costs up to 3.99% plus 0.49 USD. Fees from marketplaces vary by marketplace.

As of November 2026, withdrawing to a bank in the same country and local currency costs 1.50 USD in supported countries, and withdrawals with conversion cost 1.2% to 4%. The page says these figures are an estimate based on its most common fee structure and that fees may differ by territory or account type. It also lists receiving and paying in USDT and USDC stablecoins, without stating their fees.

Airwallex

Airwallex's US pricing is for businesses. As of November 2026, the Explore plan costs $0 a month and Grow costs $12 per active Spend user a month plus a platform fee based on team size. The monthly fee is charged per business legal entity. Conversion costs 0.5% above interbank rates for major currencies and 1% for the rest. SWIFT transfers cost $15 to $25, and domestic transfers in USD and CAD are free. Global Accounts hold funds in 20+ currencies.

OFX

For personal transfers, as of November 2026, OFX's US transfer rates page shows an OFX fee of $0.00 in its example and says your rate is the market rate plus OFX's margin. It also notes that third-party banks sometimes deduct a fee. The page gives no margin as a number.

For companies, the OFX business pricing page lists a $0 Standard plan and a $75 Full Suite plan as of November 2026. SWIFT payments cost $20 and FedWire payments $5. Standard includes 20 domestic ACH payments a month, then $0.50 each. You can receive, hold and pay in 30+ currencies, with local account details for USD, GBP, EUR and CAD. The OFX US site names its operator as USForex Inc. and gives the money transmitter number NMLS #1021624.

Bank of America

As of November 2026, Bank of America's wire page lists a $45 fee for an international wire sent in US dollars. A wire sent in a foreign currency has no wire fee, but exchange rate markups apply, and the bank says those markups are included in its exchange rate. Incoming wires may cost $15 each. The page says wires can go out in 140+ currencies and does not mention holding foreign currency balances.

Wise business alternatives

When you weigh a Wise business alternative, start from what Wise Business charges as of November 2026: its pricing page shows a 31 USD setup fee for the full set of business features, and sending and conversion fees from 0.23%.

As of November 2026, Airwallex prices by Spend user and includes free batch transfers on its Explore plan. Its pricing page also lists card issuing through an API on all plans. OFX prices by plan and user, with $10 a month for each user beyond the five in Full Suite. It includes company cards and lists 1% cashback on card spend. OFX also says it is waiving its $5 fee for receiving international payments for Standard and Full Suite clients from May 12, 2026. Payoneer prices each transaction (receiving, sending, withdrawals, conversion and cards) rather than by plan, and it is the one of the three that lists stablecoin payments.

If you need a multi-currency business account, compare the currencies with local account details first, then the cost of the payments you make most often.

Wise alternatives with stablecoin and crypto access

As of November 2026, Wise's help article says it does not support businesses involved in the exchange or trading of cryptocurrencies, and it lists limits for personal accounts too. Among the providers above, only Payoneer's pricing page mentions stablecoins. The Revolut fee schedule, Airwallex, OFX and Bank of America pages checked for this comparison do not.

Questions

Is Wise a bank?

As of November 2026, the Wise US account page describes Wise as a money services business registered with FinCEN and says it is not a bank with federal deposit insurance. Check each alternative's own site for how it describes its status.

Can you buy crypto with Wise?

Not through the account. As of November 2026, Wise's help article says it does not support the purchase, exchange or trading of cryptocurrencies, and personal customers cannot send money to crypto exchanges or to wallets built to hold crypto. The same article says Wise cards can be used for any lawful transaction supported in the card region, including on crypto platforms.

Do Wise alternatives charge to receive money?

Some do. As of November 2026, Payoneer charges nothing for payments from another Payoneer balance or into a local-currency receiving account, and 1% into a non-local one. Bank of America says incoming wires may cost $15 each. Wise lists 6.11 USD for each USD wire or SWIFT payment received.

Is there a Wise alternative for personal use?

Yes. As of November 2026, Revolut's Standard plan and OFX's personal transfers are for individuals, and a bank wire is another route. Airwallex and the OFX plans in the table are priced for businesses.
